result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.normalized_cut_size()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get the normalized cut size between two sets of nodes. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L55360-L55420){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.normalized_cut_size( S, T=None, weighted=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Normalized cut size](/assets/graphs/normalized-cut-size.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The same graph and set S, with every degree in a badge. Three edges cross the cut (accent); S holds 9 edge ends and the rest 11, so the normalized cut is 3 · (1/9 + 1/11) = 0.606." width="100%"} The cut size divided by the volume of each side and summed: `cut * (1 / vol(S) + 1 / vol(T))` (Shi & Malik, 2000). Unlike the plain cut, it penalizes lopsided splits, since slicing off a single lightly connected node gives a small cut but a tiny volume. Minimizing it is the objective behind spectral clustering and image segmentation. `T` defaults to the complement of `S`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [S]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : One set of nodes, as integer IDs or string labels. [T]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The other set. If `None` (default), all nodes not in `S`. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to use edge weights. If `None` (default), follows the graph. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The normalized cut size. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `S=` is empty, a node does not exist, or a side has zero volume. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Splitting the two triangles apart is cheap; splitting off one node is not: ::: {#b0de56c2 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E"), ("E", "F"), ("F", "D")]) ) triangle = graph.normalized_cut_size(["A", "B", "C"]) single = graph.normalized_cut_size(["A"]) round(triangle, 3), round(single, 3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (0.286, 1.167) ``` ::: :::
